findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, blocking team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, requiring both predicates means only team *owners* can pass this branch, and team admins are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and the UI (`booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`) imply admins should be allowed. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Additionally, for non-team bookings `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` performs two pointless membership queries against team id 0 on every call.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate filtering are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased when parsed from `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, but the incoming `guest` string is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). A caller can therefore bypass the blacklist entirely by sending `Blocked@Example.com` instead of `blocked@example.com`, and that address will be inserted as an attendee and emailed. The duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` has the same problem: an email that differs only in letter case from an existing attendee passes the filter and a second attendee row with the same mailbox is created. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` (and trim) before comparing/inserting.

findings.title: Input schema allows duplicate and unbounded guest lists
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no uniqueness refinement and no `.max()` limit. The uniqueness check only exists client-side in `AddGuestsDialog` (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with the Set refinement), so a direct tRPC call with `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` creates two identical attendee rows for the booking, and a call with thousands of addresses creates thousands of attendees and sends that many emails from the Cal instance (spam/abuse amplification). The server should de-duplicate and cap the list.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the *logged-in* user, but this endpoint is explicitly reachable by attendees and team admins/owners (see the permission check above). When a non-organizer adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is executed with credentials that do not include the calendar/video credential referenced by `booking.references`, so the external calendar event is not updated (or the update fails silently) and the newly added guests never appear on the organizer's calendar invite. The organizer (`booking.user`, already fetched with `credentials`) should be used to build the EventManager.

findings.title: No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
findings.body: The handler loads the booking by id only and never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. A caller can therefore add guests to a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, which inserts attendees and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with an ICS of `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` — i.e. new guests receive an invite for a meeting that no longer exists. The UI also exposes the action through `editBookingActions`, which is rendered for past bookings (`isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` branch in BookingListItem), so guests can be invited to meetings that already happened. Reject non-ACCEPTED/past bookings server-side.

findings.title: Raw input is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered guest list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered request input. `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats every address in that list as a *new* guest and sends it the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a "your booking is confirmed" email). Any address that was in the request but filtered out as an already-existing attendee therefore receives a duplicate booking-confirmation email instead of the intended "guests added" notification. `uniqueGuests` (the list actually inserted) should be passed instead.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file gates host/attendee mail on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` (see `sendLocationChangeEmails` directly above). `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` argument and performs no such check, so event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee` will still send organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating that setting. The handler should pass `booking.eventType?.metadata` and the sender should honour it.

findings.title: Booking `responses.guests` is not updated and no webhooks/workflows are triggered
findings.body: Guests are inserted only into the `Attendee` table; the booking's `responses` JSON (which holds the `guests` booking field and is the source of truth used when the booking is rescheduled or re-rendered from booking fields) is left untouched, so added guests silently disappear on reschedule and are inconsistent with what the booking form shows. The handler also fires no webhook (`BOOKING_*`) and no workflow reminders for the new attendees, unlike other mutation handlers in this router, so integrations will not see the change.

findings.title: Seated events: attendees added without BookingSeat records break seat accounting
findings.body: For event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, each attendee of a booking represents a booked seat and has an associated `BookingSeat` row (used for per-seat cancel/reschedule links and for computing remaining seats). This handler inserts plain `Attendee` rows with no `bookingSeat`, so added guests consume seats without being counted/limited, cannot cancel or reschedule their seat, and the attendee list of a seated booking can exceed `seatsPerTimeSlot`. Seated bookings should either be rejected or handled explicitly.

findings.title: findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` yields an opaque 500 for userless bookings
findings.body: `booking.userId` is nullable (e.g. dynamic group bookings or bookings whose user was deleted). In that case the query runs with `id: 0`, `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma NotFound error that is not caught, and the client receives an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful message. Handle the null `userId` explicitly (the booking's `user` relation is already included in the first query and could be reused instead of this second round-trip).

findings.title: Organizer email subject can be empty or crash on attendees[0]
findings.body: The subject interpolates `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. New guests are created with `name: ""` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, and the attendee list passed into the event is built from `prisma.booking.update(... include: { attendees: true })` with no `orderBy`, so the first element is not guaranteed to be the original booker — the subject can render as "Guests Added:  with  at ...". If `attendees` were ever empty this line throws while building the mail payload. Use a defensive fallback (e.g. `attendees[0]?.name || organizer.name`) and order attendees deterministically.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports the @calcom/ui barrel from inside packages/ui, creating a cycle
findings.body: `MultiEmail.tsx` lives in `packages/ui` but imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, which is the package's own `index.tsx` — and that index now re-exports `./form/MultiEmailLazy` → `./MultiEmail`. This circular import can produce undefined components at module-init time depending on bundler evaluation order, and it also pulls the entire UI barrel into the dynamically imported chunk, defeating the purpose of the `MultiEmailLazy` code split documented in that file. Import the components from their relative paths (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, etc.) as the other files in `packages/ui/form` do.

findings.title: Validation error state is never reset on success or dialog close
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is set in `handleAdd` but is only cleared by the Cancel button. On a successful mutation (`onSuccess`) and when the dialog is dismissed via the overlay/escape (`onOpenChange` → `setIsOpenDialog`), `isInvalidEmail` stays `true`, so the next time the dialog is opened the red "Emails must be unique and valid" message is displayed before the user has typed anything. Reset the flag in `onSuccess` and at the start of `handleAdd`.

findings.title: Clicking Add with no email rows does nothing and gives no feedback
findings.body: When the user removes all email rows, `multiEmailValue.length === 0` and `handleAdd` returns silently: no toast, no inline error, no mutation. The button looks functional but is a no-op, which reads as a broken dialog. Either disable the Add button when the list is empty or surface the validation message.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a bare console.log
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards the actual error object, so an SMTP/template failure produces no actionable information in logs (the rest of the codebase uses `@calcom/lib/logger` with `safeStringify`). Log the error itself via the logger so these failures are diagnosable.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
findings.body: This PR adds a new authenticated mutation that writes attendees, mutates external calendars and sends mail, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin-owner), blacklist filtering and de-duplication — but no unit or integration test is included. At minimum there should be tests covering: rejection for an unrelated user, acceptance for organizer/attendee/team admin, duplicate and blacklisted emails being filtered, and the emails being sent only for newly added guests.
